translations.text: Discourse of our holy and blessed father Hippolytus the archbishop: The Pattern of the Covenant.
1.1 True is this word that I speak, and worthy to be accepted with all propriety:
that we should awaken from sleep at this time and lift up our hearts upon our arms to God in the heavens, lest the householder come suddenly,
so that when he comes he may find us awake. 1.2 Let us be watchful at this time of the bridegroom, so that we may enter the wedding chamber with him;
let us make ready oil for our lamps, so that we may go out to meet him with joy;
let us prepare provisions for our stopping-places on that narrow and slender road. 1.3 Let us strip off and cast away from us all filthiness, so that we may put on the wedding garment;
let us add to the silver that we have received, so that we may be called a good and faithful servant; let us be always in prayer, so that we may pass through that place of judgment and terror;
let us purify our hearts from weakness, so that we may see the Most High in his glory;
let us become merciful, as it is written, so that God may have mercy on us; let there be peace among us, so that we may be called brothers of Christ;
let us hunger for righteousness, so that we may be filled from the table of the Lord; let us become righteous in truth, so that we may not be given as food to the serpent;
1.4 let us clear our sown field of thorns, so that we may yield fruit a hundredfold; let us lay our foundation upon the rock, so that it may not be shaken by winds and waves.
Let us become a precious vessel, useful to its Lord; let us sell our possessions and buy that pearl, Christ, so that we may become rich;
let us store up our treasure in the heavens, so that when we arrive we may open it; and 1.5 let us visit our Lord in sickness, so that he may call us and we may stand at his right hand;
let us hate ourselves and love Christ, as he loved us and gave himself up for us;
let us hold the Spirit of Christ in honor, so that we may find grace from him; let us become strangers to this world, as Christ held himself a stranger to this world;
1.6 let us become humble and meek, so that we may inherit that land of blessing; let us be diligent in his service, so that he may serve us in that tabernacle of holiness;
let us pray to him in holiness, so that we may enter into the presence of the riches of his divinity.
Let us share in his suffering, so that we may live with him in the resurrection; let us take up his mark in our flesh, so that we may escape the wrath that is to come.
Terrible is that day on which he will come, and who is there that can endure it?
Terrible and mighty is his wrath, and it will destroy all the lawless. 1.7 Now let us put on the helmet of hope, so that we may not be wounded and perish in the contest;
let us bind our loins firmly with truth and righteousness, so that we may not be found unfastened in the contest of battle;
let us rise and awaken Christ, so that he may calm this storm; let us take up the shield against the evil one, the readiness of the gospel of our Savior;
1.8 let us receive authority from the Lord, so that we may be bold to trample upon serpents and vipers; let us put away from us wrath and anger, together with all malice;
put away shameful speech and disorderly frivolity from your mouths, for with these you pray to God;
Let us not be cursers, so that we may be delivered from the curse of the law. 1.9 Let us become quick-working laborers, so that we may receive our wages along with the first ones.
Let us bear the burden of this day, so that we may receive a greater wage. Let us not be idle laborers, for behold, our Lord has brought us into his vineyard.
Let us be planted as vines in the vineyard of Christ, for he himself is the true vine.
1.10 Let us be fruit-bearing vines, so that we may not be cast out of the true vine. Let us be a fragrant scent, so that our fragrance may spread all around us.
Let us make ourselves poor in this world and make many rich by our teaching.

Let us take no father for ourselves on earth, so that we may become sons of the Father in heaven. And though we seem to have nothing, we have everything; and though it seems that no one knows us, those who know us are many.
1.11 Let us always rejoice in our hope, so that our hope and our Savior may rejoice over us.
Let us afflict ourselves in that world and become bound to share in the sufferings of the Lord, so that we may not hang our heads at meeting him, at the [?] of judgment.
Let us take up the armor of the contest, the readiness of the gospel. Let us knock at the door of heaven, so that it may be opened before us and we may enter it.
1.12 Let us ask for his mercy without wearying, so that we may receive as much as we desire. Let us seek his kingdom and righteousness, so that this earth too may be given and added to us.
Let us care for what is above and think on it, on the place to which Christ has ascended. Let us leave this world, for it is indeed not ours.
And let us press on toward that world to which we have been appointed. Let us lift up our eyes on high, so that we may see the radiance of his appearing.
1.13 Let us rise up on our wings like eagles, so that we may see with whom the body is.
Let us prepare the gift for the King, the desired fruit: fasting and prayer, which is his pledge, so that he may make us trusted over all his treasure.
And whoever is not faithful to his covenant, to what he promised, will not be permitted to enter the treasure house.

Now let us be attentive to the voice of the Bridegroom. Let us go out to meet him with joy, and let us offer him as our contribution the covenant and righteousness, and let us be faithful to the covenant.

And let us be delivered from the unquenchable fire. 1.14 But whoever is not dressed in the wedding garment will be driven out into the outer darkness and will not be permitted to eat of the wedding bread.
Whoever loves estates and trade will be found deprived [?] of the city of the saints.
And whoever does not bear fruit in the vineyard, let him be stripped and cast out to torment.
Whoever receives silver from his lord, let him return it to the one who gave it, with interest. Whoever wishes to be a merchant,
let him buy the field with money. And 1.15 whoever sows the seed of holiness, let him clear his ground of thorns.
Whoever wishes to be a hunter, let him always keep his gear ready. Whoever wishes to be holy in this world, let him keep himself with care.
Whoever wishes to receive the crown of heaven, let him be faithful to his covenant.
Whoever runs on the racecourse, let him beware of the treachery of his adversary. 1.16 Whoever enters the contest, let him arm himself firmly.
Let him who has acquired a coat of mail keep it pure at all times. Let him who takes upon himself the likeness of the angels keep himself a stranger to men.
Let him who takes up the yoke of the saints put away from himself giving and taking. Let him who wishes to find himself put away from himself the gain of this world.
Let him who loves the house of heaven not toil over houses of clay. 1.17 Let him who wishes to be lifted up with the clouds not take pains over swift mounts.
Let him who desires to see that heavenly bridegroom keep himself undefiled at all times. Let him who desires that heavenly cup keep away from drunkenness.
Let him who has chosen for himself the bread of the heavenly bridegroom not go off to trade in this world. 1.18 Let him who has sown good seed for himself keep it clean of tares and thorns.
Let him who begins to build a tower calculate with what he will build it.
For he who begins to build must also finish, so that he may not become an object of reproach to those passing by.
Let him who builds a house lay its foundation with deliberation upon the rock, so that it may not be shaken by the winds.
Let him who wishes to flee from darkness walk in the light while the light is with him. Let him who fears flight in winter prepare his refuge in summer.
Let him who wishes to enter into rest prepare provisions for that Sabbath. 1.19 He who asks of the Lord the forgiveness of his debts,
let him too forgive that debtor of his. Let him who loves humility be an inhabitant of that land of the living.
He who loves peace shall be called a child of God. Let him who knows the will of his Lord do his will, so that he may not receive greater wrath.
He who purifies himself of deceit shall see Christ the King with his own eyes. 1.20 He who receives the Spirit of Christ,
let him keep himself pure and guard his inner man, which has been called the temple of God; let him keep his flesh pure from all filth.
He who grieves the Spirit of Christ shall be in sorrow at all times. He who receives the body of Christ,
let him keep his flesh pure from all impurity [?]. Let him who has stripped off the old man no longer return to those same former deeds.
Let him who has put on the new man guard himself from all filth.
Let him who has put on armor from the water of the baptismal font not take it off, so that he may not be condemned.
Let him who takes up a shield against the attacker guard himself from the arrows coming at him.
He who is lazy is not pleasing before his Lord. 1.21 Let him who meditates on the law of the Lord not fall into the thinking of this world.
He who wills to walk in the law of the Lord is like a tree planted beside the watercourse.
He who puts his hope in mortal man shall receive the curse that Jeremiah spoke.
Let him who lights his lamp not put it out. Let him who awaits the voice of the bridegroom take oil with him.
And let him who is doorkeeper be watchful for his lord. Let him who loves virginity be like Elijah.
Let him who takes up the yoke of the covenant fulfill that covenant. Let him who loves a life of restraint wait in hope.

2.1 Crafty, brothers, and full of many devices is that attacker of ours, and he prepares himself against the face of the valiant in order to undo them; the weak are already his, and he does not fight those whom he has taken captive,
but those who have the wings of righteousness fly up by means of them, and his arrow cannot reach them when he shoots at them.
The spiritual see him when he fights, and they do not let him rule over their bodies.
None of the children of light are afraid of him, for darkness flees before the face of light.
And the children of good are not afraid of evil, for it has been given over to be trampled under their feet.
2.2 For when he wars against them in the likeness of darkness, they become light; and when he hisses over them like the serpent,
they become salt, and he cannot eat of them; and if he appears to them in the likeness of an asp and a viper, they become like the children of the Ninevites.
And if he comes in against them through hunger for food, they overcome him by their fasting, like our Savior.
And if he fights them through the delight of the eyes, by this they lift up their eyes to the height of heaven. 2.3 And if he wishes
to entice them with words, they drive his word away from their ears.
And if he shows himself openly to them and makes war, they arm themselves with faith and strike him down.
And if he comes upon them by force, they rouse themselves and stay awake to worship and glorify God; and if he shakes them with possessions, they distribute what is theirs to the poor.
And if he stirs them with desire for Eve, they withdraw alone and stay apart, and not with the daughters of Eve.
3.1 He came in against Adam by the hand of Eve, and Adam was deceived in his folly.
He came against Joseph by the hand of his mistress, and Joseph perceived his guile and did not listen to the word of his mistress.
By the hand of a woman he fought against Samson, until he destroyed from him the vow that was upon him.
Reuben was the firstborn of all his brothers, and by the hand of his father's wife a blemish fell upon him. 3.2 Aaron was high priest in the house of Israel.
And on account of Miriam, his sister, he became jealous of Moses. He sent Moses to bring the people out of the land of the Egyptians, and he took along with him that counselor of evil things.
And the Lord met Moses and sought to kill him. He sent his wife back from that very place to the land of the Midianites.
David was valiant and mighty in every contest, and by the hand of a daughter of Eve guilt was found in him.
Amnon was handsome and fair to look upon, and desire for his sister bound him, and he killed him by means of Absalom, because he had defiled his sister Tamar.
3.3 Solomon was exalted and magnified above all the kings of the earth, and in the days of his greatness women turned aside his heart.
And by the hand of Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, the evil of Ahab multiplied, and he was defiled.
At the time when he tested Job through his children and possessions and could not master him, he went and came in to that daughter of Eve and approached her,
the one who overthrew Adam, and he speaks through her mouth to that righteous man Job and said to him: "Speak some word against God."
But he despised his teaching. 3.4 King Asa overcame that accursed life, at the time when his mother sought to deceive him by her own hand.
But Asa perceived her guile; he humbled his mother from her dignity, and he destroyed and crushed the idols that his mother served.
John was great among all the prophets, and Herod killed him at the dancing of the daughter of Herodias.
Haman was rich, second to the king, and his wife counseled him to destroy the Jews.
Zimri was a chief over the tribe of Simeon, and Cozbi, the daughter of the king of the Midianites, brought him to ruin.
Because of one woman, twenty-four thousand of Israel fell in one day.
4.1 Therefore, brothers, every man who for the sake of the covenant and of holiness remains alone,
let him not desire to be with a woman, nor to go inside a woman's dwelling; rather, it is better for him to have a wife openly.
And for a woman likewise it is proper that she should have a husband openly, rather than burning and sin;
let a woman associate with women and a man with men. 4.2 If a man and a woman have been joined by a blessed marriage, let them not separate.
If they have separated by a vow, let them not come together a second time, so that it may not be counted as adultery. From now on, this teaching is good and beautiful.
I have taught myself and you, beloved: the solitary life of men and the solitary life of women is good and beautiful.
Let those who have kept themselves in the covenant endure the tribulation of this world. 4.3 For Jeremiah the prophet said:
"Blessed is the man who takes up the yoke from his youth and sits in silence, for he has taken your yoke upon himself. Thus it is proper, beloved.
Whoever takes up the yoke of Christ by a vow, let him keep it in holiness.
5.1 For thus it is written of Moses, beloved: at the time when the Holy One appeared, he too loved holiness.
And at the time when he was sanctified, his wife, by the circumcision of her son, did not serve him, for thus it is written:
"Joshua son of Nun was the servant of Moses from his youth." And further, of Joshua it is thus written: "He did not depart from the tent."
And the tent of meeting was not served by the hand of a woman, for the law does not command women to enter the tent of meeting,
but when women came to worship, they would worship outside the door and go away.
And he commanded the priests thus, saying: "When the service of the tent of meeting takes place, keep yourselves pure from your wives." 5.2 And of Elijah it is thus written:
There was a time when he dwelt on Mount Carmel, and there was a time when he dwelt at the brook Cherith, and he was served by his disciple.
For his heart was in heaven; the birds of heaven brought him food, for he took upon himself the likeness of the watchers of heaven.
These same watchers brought him bread and water." And when he fled from the face of Jezebel,

he laid all his care in heaven, and he was caught up toward heaven by a chariot of fire, and there his dwelling came to be forever, through keeping the covenant. 5.3 And Elisha walked in the ways of his master.
And he stayed in the upper room of the Shunammite woman and was served by his own disciple, for thus said that Shunammite woman:
"This prophet is a holy man of God, and he is always passing back and forth here.
Now, as befits his holiness, let us make him an upper room to stay in and furnishings for his rest."
And what, then, were those furnishings for rest in Elisha's upper room?
A bed, a table and a lampstand. 5.4 And what more shall I say about John, who did not wish even to live among people, and who guarded his virginity by a vow, and who received the spirit of Elijah?
And the blessed apostle says of himself and of Barnabas: "Do we not have the right to eat and drink, or to take women along with us? But it is not proper."
6.1 Therefore, brothers, let us see and understand that from the beginning the enemy entered into man by the hand of a woman, and until the end he fights us by the same means.
She is the devil's instrument, and by her hand he fights the elect of God; and she became for him a mouth and [?] on the first day;
because of her the curse of the law was laid down; because of her death entered: in pain she bears children, and they are given over to death;
because of her the earth was cursed, so that thorn and thistle should spring up. 6.2 From then on, at the coming of blessed Mary, the thorn was torn away,
the sweat was wiped away, the fig tree was cursed, the dust became salt, the curse was nailed to the wood of the cross, paradise has been announced to the blessed saints,
the tree of life has been given as food to the faithful and the willing, virgins offer fruit, the door is opened, the way is cleansed, a spring has welled up and gives drink to the thirsty,
the wedding chamber is opened, the fatted ox is slaughtered, the cup of life is mixed, joy is spread out, the apostles are sending invitations;
those invited are many. 6.3 You who are invited, keep yourselves ready: the bridegroom [?]!
A good light has shone forth, and a beautiful, unfading adornment has been prepared; the herald has drawn near and cries out,
the tombs are opened, hidden things are revealed, the dead rise, the trumpet sounds, the sound of the lyre is heard,
these living ones fly up to meet the Lord, the watchers in the heavens hasten, the throne of judgment is set up.
Whoever has labored rejoices; whoever has grown weak is afraid. 6.4 Let the youths on the right side be joyful, and let those on the left mourn and weep.
Those who lie in darkness sigh; those who are in the light rejoice.
Grace has appeared, truth reigns; there is no repentance in that world. Summer has drawn near to us, winter has gone far from us.
The Sabbath of rest has arrived, light reigns, the goad of death flees. 6.5 Whoever has been found steadfast in the vow rejoices, delights and gives praise.
Those who have not taken wives will be served by the watchers of heaven.
And those who have taken wives, or if a woman has a husband, and they keep faith with each other in the vow, will be made worthy of the heavenly crown;
let the keepers of the vow rejoice in the house of the Most High. And may the Only-Begotten, who came from the bosom of the Father, give joy to all who live alone.
There is no distinction there between male and female, nor between slave and master, for all will be offspring of God. 6.6 And to all the holy virgins,
Those who have betrothed themselves to Christ will there kindle their lamps and enter the bridal chamber before the bridegroom.
All who have believed in Christ are far from the curse of the law, and they are outside the punishment of the daughters of Eve;

they are far from the pain of childbirth, and they have counted the having of children in this world as nothing, nor do they worry about their livelihood, but they put their trust in Christ by that vow.
And because they do not go to a husband, the name gives them more joy than sons and daughters. 6.7 And instead of the mourning of the daughters of Eve, they sing to God with psalm and praise.
The wedding of the daughters of Eve lasts seven days, but that of the holy virgins lasts to the end of the ages.
The adornment of the daughters of Eve is of wool and [?], which wears out and passes away, but the garment of the virgins will not wear out forever.
Old age withers the beauty of the daughters of Eve, but the beauty of those who keep the vow will be renewed and will shine at the time of the resurrection.
7.1 O virgin, you who have betrothed yourself to Christ, should anyone speak to you and say:
"Come, stay with me and serve me," answer him this way: "I am betrothed to a man who is a king; him I serve, and for him I keep myself with care.
If I abandon him and his service, he will grow angry with me, write a bill of divorce, and drive me out of my house.
And while you seek rest from me and I from you, let us not be found guilty and destroy that virginity of ours which we have vowed. 7.2 Beloved,
do not cast fire into your bosom, so that the wedding garment may not be burned; instead, remain alone and keep watch over your vow.

[?] the pledge, and I too will remain alone, and let us prepare oil for ourselves, so that we may enter the bridal chamber with the wise virgins and not be left standing outside with the foolish ones."
8.1 Listen, beloved, to what I am writing to you, about how those who have made a vow and holy virgins ought to conduct themselves:
First this: to hold firmly to the yoke of the faith, about which I wrote to you in the first letter,
so that you may be diligent in worship, in fasting, and in the love of Christ; and be gentle and humble, sincere in speech and pure in mind toward all people.
8.2 Let your speech be measured, and shut the door of your lips against vain words; and beware of loud laughter.
Do not love the adornment of clothing, and do not toil over your attire like a man who has a wife or like a woman who has a husband.
Do not [?] a wedding, and do not overindulge in wine. 8.3 Put a proud mind far from you, and do not desire the sight of adorned bridegrooms.
Put a deceitful tongue and lying lips far from you, and do not speak evil of anyone, and do not heed a false report until good and evil have been examined.
If you lend, do not exact interest and increase, and do not love greed. Love giving rather than receiving.
8.4 Do not reproach a person who has turned to repentance, and do not mock a brother who fasts, nor shame one who cannot fast.
In a place where they receive you, be careful, and where they do not receive you, consider
what concerns yourself. When your words are received, speak; if they are not received, be silent.
And for the sake of your belly do not make yourself contemptible by going from house to house. 8.5 Whoever fears God, to him reveal your counsel, and guard yourself from evil.
And do not speak evil in secret about a neighbor, even if he is your enemy; and labor in such a way that you have no one at all who hates you.
And if someone is envious of anyone because of a good deed, you add good all the more and to a greater degree. When you have anything, give to the poor and be joyful;
if you have nothing, do not be grieved, but keep praying for them. 8.6 And let your counsel not be with a slanderous man;
and do not be with a reviling man, so that he may not speak evil of your Lord. Do not try to please your neighbor by illusion.
All this befits solitaries and virgins, who have taken up the heavenly yoke by a vow and have become disciples of Christ.
Thus it befits them, so that they may become like Christ, their teacher.
9.1 Let us also, beloved, take on the likeness of our Savior, for he was rich and became poor, he is exalted and humbled himself.
His dwelling is on high, yet on earth no place was found where he might lay his head.
He is to come upon the clouds; he sat upon a donkey and entered Jerusalem. And though he is God and the Son of God, he took upon himself to put on the form of a servant.
9.2 And though he was the rest of all the weary, he himself grew weary, so that he might give rest to us all.
And though he was a spring and gave drink to all the thirsty, he thirsted and asked for a drink. And though he himself was fullness, he satisfied our hunger and himself grew hungry.
He went out into the desert and was tempted. Though he was wakeful and did not sleep, he slept in a boat in the midst of the sea.
And though the watchers in the heavens serve him, he who sits upon the thrones of the Father himself served people with his own hands.
9.3 And though he was the healer of all the sick, nails were driven into his hands.
And though he poured forth good with his mouth toward all, they fed him gall. And though he harmed no one, they beat him and reviled him.
And though he was the giver of life to all the dead, he gave himself over to death on the cross.
10.1 All this humility the Savior showed us. From now on let us too humble ourselves, brothers.
When our Lord came outside his own nature, he also lived among us clothed in this nature of ours.
Let us stand and wait for that nature of his in this nature of ours, so that on the day of judgment he may make us sharers in that nature of his.
Our Lord received his pledge and ascended.
He who lacked nothing did this for our fulfillment. 10.2 This of ours was indeed his already, but that of his, from where would it come to us?
Trustworthy is this word which he promised us: "Where I am, there you too shall be with me."
That which he received from us is with him in glory and honor. And it befits us all the more to keep that of his which is with us in glory and honor.
That of ours is held in honor with him; likewise let us also hold that of his in honor with us. 10.3 If we glorify that of his which is with us,
He would come to meet us with that which is ours and draw us to himself. If we treat what is his with contempt, he will take back from us what is his.
And if we neglect that pledge of his, which he promised us, he will separate us from that as well.
Let us be careful of that son of the king who is with us, for our pledge too is with him. Whoever honors that son of the king will find honor from the king.
That which is ours sits in honor with him. He set a diadem upon it and seated it at his right hand. 10.4 And we, since we are poor and dust, what shall we give in return to that son of the king?
He needs nothing from us except this: that we keep this temple holy, so that when the times are fulfilled and he brings us to the Father, we may stand before him with joyful faces, full of grace.
When he came, nothing of ours was with him, except that he put on this which is ours. 10.5 At the time when Gabriel brought the good news to blessed Mary,
from whom the Lord was born, he brought the Word from on high and came, and that Word became flesh and dwelt among us.
And when he ascended to the one who had sent him, he took up that flesh, of which he had brought nothing from there, as the apostle says:
"When he went to his Father, he raised us up and seated us in the heavens and sent us the Holy Spirit, and said:
'Receive the Holy Spirit, and I am with you until the end of the world.'" 10.6 Christ is at the right hand of the Father; Christ is among human beings;
he has power over the things above and the things below; he is the wisdom of the Father and dwells among many.
He is one, and he is found in fullness with many believers; and he was not diminished, as it is written: "He divided him among many."
Although he is divided among many, even so he sits at the right hand of the Father; and because he sits at the right hand of the Father, we are with him and he is with us, as he said:
"You are with me and I am among you." And again he said: "I and my Father are one."
11.1 If someone's mind is too weak to understand, he will take a stand and dispute this saying, and say: "Christ is one and his Father is one.
So how can the Father and the Son dwell with a believing person?" You, believer, answer: The names of the Trinity are individual, but the equality of the Trinity is:
one nature, one divinity, one essence, one power, in unity with all believing people.
There are not many gods, nor countless Christs, but three names: the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
One God over all forever, amen. 11.2 Listen, beloved, how the word may be understood from things that are visible.
All that is created can be known, but no one can tell the essence of the Creator, nor is anyone able to search it out.

It is plain to everyone that the disc of the sun is in the heavens and its light is spread over the earth, and from it light enters through the many doors of a house and comes in through the windows of many temples.
And wherever its brilliance goes, it is called the sun. Even if it is only as much as a man's [?] and has entered into any crevices whatever, it is still called the sun.
And the disc of the sun remains in the heavens and is not diminished, and they are not said to be many suns. 11.3 And the waters of the sea are many, and if I draw even a single cupful from the sea,
it is still called water; and if I fill a thousand vessels, it is called the same, and nothing is lost from the sea.
In the same way, you may light a candle from a fire, and that fire loses nothing. And if you take some of it for kindling, it remains just the same.

And if you take up earth from the ground, you cannot change its name. 11.4 In the same way also God and his only-begotten Son and his Holy Spirit are with many believing people, and he remains in his own divinity.
If the orb of the sun is not diminished when it spreads over the earth, if this is so, far greater is the power of God.
12.1 Further, let me remind you, beloved, of the Scriptures. At the time when Moses had grown heavy with old age and could not manage the people, the Lord said to him:
"I will take of that Spirit of yours which is with you and spread it upon seventy elders." And he took of the Spirit of Moses and filled seventy men with it, and Moses lacked nothing,
nor was the Holy Spirit that was with him diminished at all. 12.2 And the blessed Apostle says:
"God apportioned of the Spirit of Christ and spread it upon the prophets," and Christ remains the same, for the Father did not give him his Spirit by measure. By this know,
beloved, that Christ dwells in many, 12.3 is divided among many, and is in fullness with the Father.
Many prophets received of his Spirit, as far as they were able, and further, of his Spirit it has been spread upon all flesh.
And their sons and their daughters prophesy, their old men and their young men, their male slaves and female slaves; and Christ is with us, and Christ is in the heavens,
at the right hand of his Father. 12.4 And Christ did not receive the Spirit by measure, but the Father loved him and gave everything into his hands.
For John says: "The Father did not give the Spirit to his Son by measure, but loved him and gave him everything"; 12.5 and the Lord himself says:
"All things have been given to me by my Father." And again he said: "The Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to his Son."
And the Apostle says: "All things shall be subjected to Christ, except the Father, who subjected all things to him.
And let God be all in all and over every person."
13.1 Concerning John our Lord testifies and says: "John is greater than all the prophets":
yet he received the Spirit by measure; by that same measure Elijah received the Spirit, and so John too had the same Spirit.
The Spirit would carry Elijah off here and there, now to the mountains, now to the deserts, now to the caves. Birds fed Elijah, and John ate winged locusts.
Elijah was girded with a belt of mantle-cloth, and John with one of leather. 13.2 Jezebel persecuted Elijah, and Herodias persecuted John. Elijah rebuked Ahab, and John rebuked Herod.
Elijah split and divided the Jordan, and John opened the font of baptism. The Spirit of Elijah rested double upon the head of Elisha.
And as for the hand of John, when it reached the head of our Savior, that same Spirit of his came upon him without measure.
For Elijah the heavens opened and he ascended, and John saw the heavens opened and the Spirit of God descending and resting upon the head of our Savior.
13.3 Elisha received a double Spirit from Elijah, but upon the Lord it came without measure from above at his baptism.
Elisha took the mantle of Elijah, and our Lord took upon himself the hand of that high priest.
Elisha made the bitter water sweet, but our Lord turned water into wine.
Elisha satisfied a hundred men with one loaf, but our Lord satisfied five thousand with five loaves, apart from women and children.
Elisha cleansed the afflicted Naaman, but our Lord cleansed the ten men.
Elisha cursed the children and bears devoured them, but our Lord blessed the children. 13.4 The children mocked Elisha, but they praised and blessed our Lord.
Elisha cursed Gehazi, but our Lord cursed Judas and blessed the apostles.
Elisha raised one dead person, but our Lord raised many dead.
Elisha lay down upon the dead child and raised him, but our Lord went down into the grave and saved and raised many.
Now, there are many miracles that the Spirit of Christ performed by the hand of the prophets and apostles.
14.1 Therefore, my brothers, we too, who have received the Spirit of Christ, and with whom Christ has made his dwelling, as it is written,
as the Holy Spirit said through the mouth of the prophets: "I will dwell with them and I will be among them":
from now on let us prepare this temple for the Spirit of Christ and let us not grieve it, so that it may not depart from us. 14.2 Let us remember how the apostle commands us, saying:
"Do not distress the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were baptized, on the day of your redemption."
For by this baptism we receive the Spirit of Christ. For when the priests invoke the Holy Spirit, when they stand at the baptismal font,
the heavens open, and it descends and rests upon the water of the font. 14.3 The Holy Spirit is far from all those born of human beings,
but when a person goes down into the font of baptism, at that moment the Holy Spirit enters that person and is with him.
In the first birth a person is formed in his mother's womb by a living breath, and afterward he is mortal.
But in the second birth, by the font, by baptism, he is immortal.
For in the font the person receives the Spirit of God, which is immortal. 14.4 And when a person dies,
he is buried in the earth, his natural place, and awareness is taken from him, and the Holy Spirit that was with him goes up to Christ.
The blessed apostle shows us these two, saying: "The natural body is buried and the spiritual body rises";
and that Spirit returns there to Christ. Again the apostle says: "When we go out from this body,
the Spirit will go to our Lord." 14.5 And the natural breath remains on the earth, and understanding is taken from it.
But whoever keeps the Spirit of Christ in holiness, when that Spirit enters before Christ, it speaks thus:
"The body into which I entered, which put me on from the water of the font, has kept me holy."
Then the Holy Spirit urges Christ that, at the resurrection of his body, he may receive greater power and glory in his body.
14.6 But the man who receives the Holy Spirit from the water of the font and grieves it: the Spirit goes out and departs from him,
while that man has not yet died, and it goes to its own nature, to Christ, and complains before Christ about the man
who grieved it. 14.7 And when the end of the times comes and the time of the resurrection arrives, the Spirit will come with mighty power and stand over the grave
in which that righteous man lies buried, the man who kept the Holy Spirit in purity; and it keeps watch for the voice from on high.
14.8 And when the watchers open the gates of heaven before the King, then the pipe blows and the lyre sounds, and the Spirit hears that sound.
And very quickly it goes and opens the grave and raises up its own body that had been hidden there,
and that glory which had gone out from it is put upon it, and the Spirit comes to be within the body that it raised.
And the glory becomes an adornment on the outside, and joyfully, in glory, he stands before Christ.
14.9 And that man becomes wholly spirit, and death is destroyed by the life of the Spirit. And he flies up by the Spirit to meet the King.
And the King will receive him with joy. And Christ is grateful to those bodies that kept purity.
15.1 Now, beloved, this Holy Spirit, which the prophets received and we also, is not with us at all times,
and there is a time when it goes to the one who sent it. 15.2 Hear, beloved, what our Lord said:
"Do not despise one of the little ones who believe in me, for their angels continually see in heaven the face of my Father."
15.3 This same Spirit goes and stands before God, and the angels see his face.
But whoever defiles the temple in which it dwelt, it complains about him before God.
16.1 And I will show you, beloved, from the Scriptures, that the Spirit is not [always] with the man to whom it belongs, as follows.
It is written of Saul: "The Holy Spirit went up from him," the Spirit that had come to him at the time of his anointing, for Saul grieved it.
And God sent him in its place an evil spirit. And when the evil spirit tormented him, David would bring the lyre before him and sing,
and at once the Holy Spirit would come, which David had received at the time of his anointing, and the evil spirit that tormented Saul would flee from before it.
16.2 And there was a time when the Holy Spirit would depart from David also, and David would take the lyre and begin to sing, and the Holy Spirit would come and rest upon him.
If the Holy Spirit had been with him always, he would not have gone astray with the wife of Uriah.
But at the time when David was bowing down and confessing his sins before God, he said this:
"Create a pure heart in me, O God, and do not take your Holy Spirit from me.
Give me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me with the spirit of your sovereign power." 16.3 And of Elisha it is written thus:
until the singer came to him with the lyre, the Holy Spirit told him nothing;
As he was playing and singing on the harp, then the Holy Spirit came to him, and he began to prophesy and said:
"Thus says the Lord: There will be no wind, nor will you see rain, yet the pools of this plain will be filled with water."
And again, when the Shunammite woman came to Elisha on account of her dead son, Elisha said this:

"And the Lord has hidden it from me and has not revealed it to me." 16.4 And again, when the king of Israel sent to have him killed, the Holy Spirit told him while the messenger had not yet come to him.
And Elisha said: "Behold, that son of the lawless one has sent to take off my head."
And again he announced the abundance that was to come to the city of Samaria after that day.
In the same way the Holy Spirit also informed him about Gehazi, that he had stolen the silver and hidden it.
17.1 Therefore, beloved, when the Holy Spirit departs from the man with whom it has been,
until the coming of that man, the evil spirit, the devil, wars against him in order to lead him astray, and when it finds that man negligent.
For as long as the Holy Spirit is still with that man, the evil spirit is afraid to approach him.
17.2 See, beloved, that our Lord, who was born of that same Spirit, was not tempted by the devil.
But when the Holy Spirit descended upon him at his baptism in the holy font of the Jordan,
afterward the evil spirit took him up onto the mountain and tempted him. 17.3 These are the wiles of the Adversary.
But you, beloved, when you sense his attack and you are not fervent in spirit and you wrap your mind in the care of this world, understand that the Spirit of God has moved far from you.
But you, arise, bow down and pray, and the Holy Spirit, your guardian, will come to you again, and your Adversary will not overcome you,
17.4 for a thief cannot dig through the wall as long as the householder is at home and awake. But when he is not found at home, or if he is asleep.
In the same way the devil cannot gain mastery over the temple of Christ, this body of ours, unless the Spirit of Christ has departed from us.
17.5 The thief knows for certain about the householder, whether he is at home or not, but he first spies and listens.
If he hears the voice of the householder as he instructs his household, saying:
"I am going away on a long journey," then when he has gone, the thief comes, digs through the wall, and steals the valuables.
If the householder is awake and warns his household to be careful, the thief is afraid and flees. 17.6 So it is also with the devil:
it is not that he has any foreknowledge by which he might know when the guardian Spirit departs from a man, but he waits for the right time and watches the man in whom Christ dwells.
And when that man speaks obscene and filthy words, or his heart grows wrathful, or he is enraged, or he quarrels with someone,
or he has fallen into a vain thought, then the devil knows that Christ is not with him, and he comes and carries out his will with him.
17.7 For Christ dwells with the meek and humble and with those who fear his words, as the prophet says:
"To whom shall I look, or with whom shall I dwell, except with the meek and the humble and those who fear my words?"
And our Lord said: "Whoever walks in my commandments and keeps my love, to him we shall come, I and my Father, and we shall make our dwelling with him."
And when he sees that man vigilant and diligent in worship and prayer, he turns away from him and does not dare to approach him.
He sees that Christ is with him. 17.8 If you say: "How many devils are there, for behold, he fights against many?"
Listen and be persuaded, and remember what I wrote above and gave you concerning Christ: that he is divided among many, and nothing of him is diminished.
In houses into which a little sun enters through a window, the whole house is lit up;
and the man into whom a little from the devil enters is himself darkened. 17.9 Listen to what the apostle says:
"If the devil appears even in the image and light of an angel, it is no great thing, for his servants also behave in the same way, as servants of righteousness."
And our Lord said to his disciples: "Behold, I have given you authority to trample all the power of the enemy."
17.10 And the books tell us that he has a great host and that he has servants, and Job says of him: "God made him an assailant [?]."
And those who are his servants he has sent out, and they run through all the world and fight against people, in order to lead them astray.
But they cannot fight openly, for authority has been given to us over him, to overcome him by the cross of Christ and by keeping our bodies pure; instead he snatches by seizure and steals by stealth.
18.1 Be persuaded by me, beloved, concerning the saying that the apostle spoke, in which the heretics go astray.
The apostle says: "There is a soulish body and there is a spiritual body.
Thus it is written, that the first man, Adam, was made a living soul, but the second Adam a living spirit." 18.2 And they go astray and say that there are two Adams, and he said:
"As we have put on the image of the Adam from the earth, so likewise we shall put on in likeness the image of the heavenly Adam."
The Adam from the earth is the one who sinned; the Adam from heaven is the Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ. 18.3 Whoever loves the Spirit of Christ
will become like that heavenly Adam, who is our Savior Jesus Christ, for that spiritual one put on this soulish one,
as I wrote to you above. 18.4 The man who afflicts the Spirit of Christ will be found soulish at the resurrection, for the heavenly Spirit will not be with him.
And when he rises, he will remain in his own nature, upon the earth, stripped of the Holy Spirit.
And because he kept the Spirit of Christ in defilement, he will be found on that day of the encounter naked, full of shame and exposed.
18.5 But whoever keeps that Spirit in honor and guards it in purity, on that day of the encounter the Holy Spirit will protect him.
And he will be complete in everything and will not be naked, as the apostle says: "Only this: when we are clothed, may we not be found naked." 18.6 And then he said:
"All of us shall fall asleep, but at the resurrection not all of us shall be renewed, for this mortal must put on immortality and this corruptible must put on incorruption.
And when this mortal has put on immortality and this corruption has put on incorruption, then the word that was written shall be fulfilled: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."

Then it says: "In the moment of the twinkling of an eye the dead shall rise incorruptible, and we shall be renewed." 18.7 And those who are renewed shall put on the image of the spiritual Adam and become spiritual,
but those who are not renewed shall remain on the earth in a fleshly, soulish state, like Adam who was from the earth.

Those who believed the promise shall be caught up to heaven, and the Holy Spirit, whom they have put on, shall make them fly upward, and they shall inherit the kingdom that was prepared for them from eternity.
And these soulish people shall remain here on the earth, in the heaviness of their flesh.
And they shall be turned away to hell. There shall be weeping of eyes and gnashing of teeth.
19.1 I have written this and have reminded myself and you, beloved.
From now on love virginity, the portion of heaven, and let all flesh keep what it has vowed, for this is the good portion; there is nothing that is equal to it.
This is union with the watchers of heaven. Christ makes his dwelling with such as these. 19.2 The time of summer has come; the branches of the fig tree have grown tender.
The signs of which our Lord spoke are coming to pass, for he said: "Nation shall rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom,
and there shall be famine and sword and death, and terrors shall appear from heaven." Behold, all this is being fulfilled in our days.
20.1 Now read this which I have written to you, you and your brothers who have made a vow and have loved virginity.
And let all who fear God, who make vows to him, keep their vow.
For it says: "Vow and fulfil your vows to the Lord your God; beware of all negligence, and meditate on the law of the Lord day and night."
20.2 Put away from your mouth shameful speech and insolence, which make a person blameworthy and expose him to disgrace, for upon such people is fulfilled that word
which is written in the Gospel, when our Lord wished to wipe away avarice from the Pharisees: "For they were lovers of money, and they derided him."
So too now, all who do not take it upon themselves to carry out these written words have derided them, just like the Pharisees. 20.3 But you,
beloved, read and learn, and set your heart on doing and fulfilling the law of the Lord; let it be your meditation and your care at all times.
And when you have read this book through, I entreat you by that life of yours.
Beloved, arise and bow down before the Lord, and remember me, a sinner, in your holy prayer.
And let us all together utter the praise and glory of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever, amen.
Holy Hippolytus, be an intercessor for Father John before our Lord Jesus Christ.
This one book was written at their expense. You who read it, pray for them.
